HRA Analysis: OVERVIEW: This is a very competitive event to open the meeting at Ballarat. COLOSIMO (9) is a lightly raced runner for the Lawlor stable. Although he has won only once, he looks a promising type with plenty of ability. He is first-up since June but has the best sectional times on exposed form in this event. Barrier nine suits fresh, as he won’t need to be used up early. MASTER LOUEY (4) is a well-bred, consistent colt for Jayne Davies. He ran a nice third in the Vicbred Super Series 3yo Colts and Geldings Bronze two starts ago. He appeared to hang out up the straight at Cranbourne last start when racing in tight quarters. With the right run, he is a winning chance. WINGATE GUY (3) is an experienced horse who is racing well and rarely puts in a bad run. He can make his own luck. BLUE MIKI (2) has found his best form recently and is progressing nicely. His good gate speed should allow him to map well here. Also respecting EL LAZZAR (11), who was impressive winning first-up for Lochie Cook last start, and FLIGHT LOUTENANT (6), who is first-up here for Jess Tubbs. BACK: COLOSIMO (9)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: COLOSIMO (9),MASTER LOUEY (4), WINGATE GUY (3), BLUE MIKI (2).

OVERVIEW: CALABASAS (10) is a trotter with a few quirks, but she has ability. Last start, she showed her best, looping the field late and hitting the line strongly to win. She will need to overcome a tricky barrier here, but she is racing well. NIGHT FLIGHT (7) is in career-best form. He is a nice trotter who usually relies on his great gate speed to map well early. However, with fast beginner Champagnes drawn to his inside, he may need to adopt different tactics and step outside his usual racing pattern. NO TELLING HEATHER (8) is in great form, having won her last two starts. Barrier eight is awkward, though. Also respecting KAMARAN (9) as he is a tough horse and has an ideal barrier to follow through early. The emergency TICTOK (11), is would be a winning chance if she gains a start. CHAMPAGNES (6) got it wrong with her manners last start, but she is a nice mare. Her good gate speed should allow her to map well here. BACK: CALABASAS (10) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:CALABASAS (10), NIGHT FLIGHT (7), NO TELLING HEATHER (8), KAMARAN (9)

OVERVIEW:HEAVENLY GEM (5) is a talented filly who looks to have an exciting future. She was brilliant throughout the Vicbred Super Series and has followed that up with two nice placings. However, she was a little rough last start, and that could be her undoing if it happens again here. HOSO MAGIC (1) has been racing well and has shown promise. Barrier one should allow her to get a good trip. WHITEHAVEN BOY (2) is an interesting runner. He began his career in the Vicbred Super Series, where he performed well. He was beaten just over 14 metres in his second career start in a Vicbred semi-final, which was a smart effort for a horse with so little experience. He was a good third last start and looks promising. ULTIMATE DELITE (3) finished an OK fourth in her first and only career start. She should improve with race fitness and experience. BACK: HEAVENLY GEM (5) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:HEAVENLY GEM (5), HOSO MAGIC (1), WHITEHAVEN BOY (2), ULTIMATE DELITE (3)

OVERVIEW: WICHITA KANSAS (9) got back into the winner’s circle nicely last start at this track. He settled in the 1-1 and hit the line well. He will likely map in a similar position here. PICKLE IT (7) has a tricky barrier but has notably the best sectional times in this field based on some of his runs this preparation. With luck, he is a winning chance. THE REGULATOR (4) has been racing well and rarely puts in a bad run. He hit the line nicely last start but was too far back. If he can map well, he should be close again. SIR CANDY CLOUD (1) has the gate speed and the ace barrier to his advantage here. SELECTIONS:WICHITA KANSAS (9), PICKLE IT (7), THE REGULATOR (4), SIR CANDY CLOUD (1)

OVERVIEW: ASONGOFTHEHEART (2) is a promising young trotter for Katrina Fitzpatrick. He has recorded two nice thirds from his two career starts to date. This is his first front-row barrier, and he looks unlikely to remain a maiden for long. WEDGE TAIL EAGLE (8) is a lightly raced gelding who has shown promise at times. He let down impressively from well back last start. LEZAMA (1) can get it wrong with her manners, but when she trots well, she looks to have something to offer. Barrier one suits if she can trot throughout. ITALIAN THUNDER (3) has got it wrong with his manners at every career start, although his trial before racing was promising. He is a winning chance if he trots throughout. BACK: ASONGOFTHEHEART (2) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: ASONGOFTHEHEART (2), WEDGE TAIL EAGLE (8), LEZAMA (1), ITALIAN THUNDER (3)

OVERVIEW: RIDDLEMETHIS (6) was first-up last start and finished second at Kilmore. He looped the field late from last and stormed home in a very close finish. He should improve with fitness. HOME AND DRY (4) was below his best last start, dropping back to last late at Ballarat. His previous runs were good, and if he can bounce back to his best here, he will be prominent. Similarly, TOMMYS LOOKOUT (5) was a little below his best last start after a tough run. He worked hard to find a position but tired late. He is usually a horse who can make his own luck, and if he finds his best form, he is a winning chance. SKYZ ABOVE (7) has a good turn of foot when saved for one run. She also has good gate speed and is usually at her best when she can find the fence, but that may be difficult from barrier seven. SELECTIONS: HOME AND DRY (4), TOMMYS LOOKOUT (5), RIDDLEMETHIS (6), SKYZ ABOVE (7)

OVERVIEW: BILLYS TIGER KHAN (2) is an exciting performer with plenty of ability. He is lightly raced, having had only 12 starts since 2024, but hasn’t raced for more than 440 days. His ability suggests he can be very competitive here, although fitness is the main query. THINKFAST RUNFAST (1) is another runner resuming after a long break, having been away from racing for 420 days. He has gate speed and has shown ability, but like Billys Tiger Khan, his lack of race fitness could be his undoing. EXOTIC CHESTER (6) is having his sixth career start and appears to be improving with each run. He led last start and was narrowly beaten late, although barrier six is awkward here. JUST PEDRO (4) covered an extra 40 metres while racing wide last start and was beaten only 7.5 metres. He is racing well but has been a little unlucky with his race map. SELECTIONS:BILLYS TIGER KHAN (2), THINKFAST RUNFAST (1), EXOTIC CHESTER (6), JUST PEDRO (4)

OVERVIEW: DREAMS FOREVER (4) is a two-year-old filly who raced in the breeze for the final lap on a rain-affected track against older mares last start and tired a little late. Although beaten 17.7 metres, it was still a respectable effort. She competed in the Vicbred Super Series prior to that and is racing better than her numerical form suggests. THEROUX (1) is a little below his best form but certainly isn’t running bad races. He hit the line well last start after settling well back early and can turn his form around from barrier one. FREAK OUT (2) was searching for racing room late last start but let down nicely once clear. He has a good barrier here and the gate speed to hold a forward position. Also respecting SUPER CODE (5), who has been racing well and isn’t afraid to make his own luck. SELECTIONS: DREAMS FOREVER (4), THEROUX (1), FREAK OUT (2), SUPER CODE (5) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:AUSSIE JAY MAC (1) broke stride at the 300m mark and lost approximately 15m before finishing off quickly when an unlucky third (7m) behind My Mate Ace at Shepparton last outing. He has performed well at the trials since and he will take beating if he gives a fool proof display. WICKED HANGOVER (6) is resuming since a Mildura victory in June but he was runner up at a recent Horsham trial effort and should be competitive against this line up. HUNGRY HOGARTH (7) will appreciate a significant drop back in class for this assignment and should go well. He performed a little below expectations when sixth at Charlton last outing but he has been freshened since and his form prior was sound. HALF PRICE BRIDE (2) is drawn to receive an economical trip and is a minor place possibility. BACK: AUSSIE JAY MAC (1) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: AUSSIE JAY MAC (1), WICKED HANGOVER (6), HUNGRY HOGARTH (7), HALF PRICE BRIDE (2)

OVERVIEW:FEEL THE REIGN (3) settled in eighth position, trailed into the race out three horses wide and hit the line strongly for third behind Altius in a mile rate of 1.56.2 at Kilmore last outing. He produced a strong finish to win at Melton prior and he looms as one of the leading chances again. SPORTING RAGE (2) is a fast beginner and performs best over the sprint distance so he has the conditions to suit him here. He won from behind the leader at Charlton on August 17. SPRINGFIELD RIVER (1) is resuming since a seventh at Cranbourne in June. He will be fitter after two recent trial performances, the latest being a second at Bacchus Marsh and he should receive a nice trip from the pole position. THIS TIME (4) is a former New South Wales pacer, which performed well for a close second at a recent Maryborough trial effort. She made her local debut when she tired late and was unplaced at Maryborough on Monday but she could improve under these conditions. SELECTIONS: FEEL THE REIGN (3), SPORTING RAGE (2), SPRINGFIELD RIVER (1), THIS TIME (4)

OVERVIEW: LATHER ME UP (1) settled on the markers and failed to run on in a heat of the Breeders Challenge at Menangle last week. She was placed in the Group 1 Bathurst Gold Tiara back in March and she is ideally drawn so she appears to be very well placed against this line up. QUEENS BOULEVARD (4) began quickly and worked forward to find the lead when a strong second behind Keayang Hustler at Horsham. She led throughout at a Stawell victory on September 14 and should give another forward showing from her good draw. TOORAM DANNY (6) settled midfield and came out three horses wide from the 600m when a close second at his first run since June. He should strip fitter from that performance and is capable of going one better. YOU’VE BEEN SERVED (5) won easily at Mildura four starts ago and has taken on strong opposition at her past three attempts, the latest being at Globe Derby where she settled down last, tried to sustain a long run and got into third before peaking late. She appears to be better placed under these conditions and is worth thought. OUR PINUP GIRL (7) produced a big performance to score in a mile rate of 1.55.7 at Ballarat then finished unplaced in a strong race at Melton. She is poorly drawn but should be finishing off well. BACK: LATHER ME UP (1) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: LATHER ME UP (1), QUEENS BOULEVARD (4),TOORAM DANNY (6), YOU’VE BEEN SERVED (5)

OVERVIEW: BENNIE AND THE JETS (9) hasn’t raced since July and hasn’t been to the trials but he is clearly the class runner of the field. He won the Elmore and Cobram Cups when he was last in work and was also placed in the Bendigo and Gunbower Cups. OFF YOUR FACESKI (8) produced a strong performance to win under the standing start conditions at Terang last outing. He is a versatile trotter and should give another bold showing. QUEEN KIZEN (5) boasts a consistent standing start record and finished a close second behind Scar at Geelong two starts ago. She performs best when she gains cover close to the pace so commencing from the handicap of 20m is a disadvantage but she is racing too well to dismiss. KENNYWOULD (4) is returning from New South Wales and will be fitter after three placed efforts at the trials. He was a runaway winner at Menangle two starts ago so he cannot be underestimated. SELECTIONS: BENNIE AND THE JETS (9), OFF YOUR FACESKI (8), QUEEN KIZEN (5), KENNYWOULD (4)

OVERVIEW:MILEY KAY (2) finished off nicely when third behind Kings Gallery on debut then had little luck when taking on a strong field in a heat of the Super Series. This is a much easier assignment and she is sure to attract plenty of support. MEGALODON (1) followed the markers throughout when placed at his first two race track appearances then attempted to make ground out wide on the track from the 500m at his latest fifth. He is perfectly drawn to suit his racing pattern and should be competitive under these conditions. CAZADERO (7) was safely held on debut but he settled in a rearward position and the winner Indulgeme recorded a slick mile rate of 1.55.4. He should find this race to be easier and he is a possible improver. SLOWBURN (6) is a New South Wales pacer, which boasts early speed and has claims. The debutante FEARLESS SNIPER (4) has been switched to trainer Boris Devcic after being safely held in four trial performances. He is well drawn first up and must be kept safe. BACK: MILEY KAY (2) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: MILEY KAY (2), MEGALODON (1), CAZADERO (7), SLOWBURN (6)

OVERVIEW:MAJOR LINCOLN (6) settled in a rearward position and picked up ground without threatening the winner at his latest third. He produced a strong finish to down ESPERANZA (2) at Stawell on September 14 and must be considered as one of the leading chances again. ESPERANZA (2) trailed the leader and used the sprint lane when she appeared to have every chance at her latest second behind MAJOR LINCOLN (6). She scored at Kilmore three starts ago and this race is no harder so she is worth thought again. TALKNPLAY (4) is resuming since a fourth at Bendigo in December but he ran a close second behind the handy type Aussie Jay Mac at a recent Shepparton trial effort. He strikes a suitable field first up and is not without a chance. IVE AN IDEA (5) produced a strong finishing burst when an eye-catching second last outing and cannot be left out of calculations. MASON DIXON LINE (8) finished sixth at Mildura when he was resuming but he was giving the leaders a big start and was making ground late. He should strip fitter from that run and rates as a value hope. SELECTIONS: MAJOR LINCOLN (6), ESPERANZA (2), TALKNPLAY (4), IVE AN IDEA (5)

OVERVIEW: JUSTALITTLESIP (8) has been racing against the Metropolitan open class and will appreciate competing in his easiest assignment for a long time. He was runner up behind He’s From Heaven in a swift mile rate of 1.52.2 five starts ago, which is a strong form pointer for this event. CALEXICO (9) will also appreciate a drop back in class from his recent efforts and battled on well after enduring a tough run at his latest fifth behind Fairplay. He is a strong 4yo pacer and should make his presence felt. LOUGLE (4) has been racing very well but without luck and warrants respect. He is versatile and is better drawn than his recent performances. MAXY WANTS TO PLAY (2) and EARL OF PEMBROKE (3) are both racing well enough to feature prominently in a quality field. BACK: JUSTALITTLESIP (8) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: JUSTALITTLESIP (8), CALEXICO (9), LOUGLE (4), EARL OF PEMBROKE (3)

OVERVIEW: KING SAINT (6) chased hard when a close second behind the smart pacer Ultimate Vinnie last outing. He battled on well for a close second behind Dembe (won again since) prior and he is capable of going one better here. TO THE NINES (8) ran a game race when making late ground in fast time at Melton then had no luck whatsoever after being headed off at the start at his latest Mildura third. He couldn’t have drawn worse but he is racing in career best form and deserves to break through for a win. NEW YORKER (9) was left stranded on the outside of the leader throughout and fought on well when fourth behind Mount Barker Boy at Melton last outing. He has been racing well at Metropolitan level and should be competitive under these conditions. OUR VINCENT CAN GOGH (7) didn’t have much luck at Melton last outing and is capable of showing improvement. SELECTIONS: KING SAINT (6), TO THE NINES (8), NEW YORKER (9), OUR VINCENT CAN GOGH (7)

OVERVIEW: Plenty of chances in this clash to start the night at Beckley Park, but ARZALI ROCKSTAR (7) looks ready to break through after back-to-back second placings in recent weeks. Two ago, she was trapped parked, did a power of work and was only nailed late, and then last Friday led before being out-sprinted by the handy Sandelton in a slick enough last half. The gate isn’t ideal, but she’s narrowly favoured. VIVA STORM (6) made the Group 2 final of the Vicbred Super Series for four-year-old mares before closing off nicely from last when sixth at Kilmore last week, YANKEE RAIN (10) has won her last two after recently joining the Tom Rundle barn and is an obvious threat, while Alex Hurley’s lovely grey SPUN SILVER (5) probably has the early toe to lead and should run well from there over the sprint trip. Hard race where plenty of others can win! SELECTIONS: ARZALI ROCKSTAR (7), VIVA STORM (6), YANKEE RAIN (10), SPUN SILVER (5)

OVERVIEW: MISS MUSCLE (9) is the two-year-old up against older horses, but she brings in some nice formlines for this 0/1-win event. Tom Rundle’s filly finished fourth despite a tough run in the Group 1 Vicbred Super Series final last month, before making a mistake in the Tatlow Stakes. She then ran a really good race from well back in transit for second to Night Flight at Ballarat. Good draw here and she looks the one to beat. Always had time for SHINELIKETHESUN (10), who did some very impressive things at stages last campaign but just struggled to put it all together. Freshened and back to the races, there’s a big watch on her. I think she’s above average. They look the main winning hopes, but respect is given to others such as THE PASO DOBLE (1), NO REPENTANCE (2), ALECTRONA (3) and DESERT ROYALE (6), who might have the speed to cross first-up from a break. SELECTIONS: MISS MUSCLE (9), SHINELIKETHESUN (10), ALECTRONA (3), THE PASO DOBLE (1)

OVERVIEW: Another wide-open race where a case can be made for plenty, including the consistent ALLWATFUNJINGLES (1). He’s certainly no superstar, but is very capable in this type of grade and importantly draws to settle closer to the speed than he has in recent starts. He’s been hitting the line nicely from well back in transit, including on October 2 at Melton when he was held up and flashed late to be narrowly beaten behind Met With A Shrug and CHINSKI (2). If he can settle behind the likely leader in CHINSKI (2), he should be able to give this a shake. CHINSKI (2) was caught parked last time at Kilmore and dropped out, but all his recent form is strong and he’s likely to run from the front, the first-up BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE (5) hasn’t raced since March and heads to Geelong without a trial, but possesses a good finishing burst when her manners are in check, while LOVE WHO (4) was a good winner at Shepparton in mid-August, then ran well for second at Maryborough before a tough trip and down-the-track finish at Horsham last time out. BACK: ALLWATFUNJINGLES (1) – 1.5 units (each-way) SELECTIONS: ALLWATFUNJINGLES (1), CHINSKI (2), BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE (5), LOVE WHO (4)

OVERVIEW: BANIA (2) steps out on debut here for David Barbetti and Mick Stanley, and I suspect he can make a winning start in this maiden event. He beat the handy Magellan in a trial at Maryborough back in July and then ran really well in a subsequent hit-out at Melton when closing off nicely from last to be beaten 5.6m in a 57.3 last half. He then won his most recent effort back at Maryborough on October 4. Happy his way. RIDE HIGH CAPTIN (8) brings clearly the best form into this maiden assignment, with runner-up placings from his last two outings. Two back, he led and was run down by the smart King Baldwin with a big margin back to third, and then wobbled around the corner at Ballarat, regained the lead and was nailed late by Ultimate Grange. He has won a Bacchus Marsh trial since and looks sure to go close in this. The others would surprise. BACK: BANIA (2) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: BANIA (2), RIDE HIGH CAPTIN (8), KATUNTI (7), SONOFPLATINUM (1)

OVERVIEW: He’s not the horse you’d bet your last dollar on, but COLTRANE (4) is one that might give you some thrills as he’s a quirky customer with loads of ability who will be very good when he puts everything together. He ruined his chances with a gallop when favourite in a 0W/15.0K stake race before a spell and has come back with two nice trials, including one where he was only 3.5m off unbeaten star two-year-old Verbici. He’s won four from 18 and there looks to be some serious scope there. EL TORNADO (5) took a while to warm up this campaign but has won his last two in really nice style at Melton and Ballarat, lightly-raced five-year-old LORD LOGAN (6) is back in Victoria after an early gallop at Globe Derby took him out of winning contention on October 3 and he’s capable of returning to winning form, while KYVALLEY JETSTREAM (7) hasn’t shown much in two runs back from a break but has ability and is dropping in grade. BACK: COLTRANE (4) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: COLTRANE (4), EL TORNADO (5), LORD LOGAN (6), KYVALLEY JETSTREAM (7)

OVERVIEW: SERIOUSLY SAL (2) ran second in the Vicbred Super Series two-year-old consolation two starts back at Ballarat and performed okay in a subsequent race at Melton last Friday despite being well beaten by a few rivals with good promise. This looks much easier, and from the good draw she must be rated a good chance. THE WOOL BROKER (4) started favourite first-up from a break at Ballarat on September 16, taking off in the last lap before getting tired and breaking. It’s hard to know how he was travelling when he made a mistake, but the form in his prior campaign was good and he’s surely good enough to win a maiden soon. NONREMARKABLE (1) hasn’t shown a great deal at the trials despite winning his last one but gets the services of James Herbertson, while the well-named WHEREDASUNDONTSHINE (3) – who is out of the mare Gluteus Maximus – is maybe next best but the others could all fill the minor end of the prize without surprising. SELECTIONS: SERIOUSLY SAL (2), THE WOOL BROKER (4), NONREMARKABLE (1), WHEREDASUNDONTSHINE (3)

OVERVIEW: ROSBERG (3) was a very good winner for this grade of horse in a race at Melton two starts ago when sitting parked, putting away the leader and then hanging on for victory. He was trapped in the same spot last time out at Ballarat, put away the leader again, but faded late to be beaten 10.7m in what was a solid run. Not sure he gets it any easier here, but I think he’ll be hard to stop regardless of where he ends up in the run. KEAYANG HUSTLER (6) is the obvious, and sometimes the obvious is the best way to go. He’s had two starts for two good wins, and while the times haven’t been off the charts by any means, the trotting-bred son of Bold Eagle is sure to be going close. BRAVE ART (1) has had two runs for smart trainer Carson Millar, with her latest being an encouraging front-running display at Ballarat when only grabbed late. Gate one, sprint trip – tick, tick. LENARD ESS (4) is set to step out for his 200th career start, and he’s the other one with a good chance.
